title: The whole server
caption: A client talks to a forked backend, SQL flows through four stages, pages move between shared buffers and disk, and WAL plus helper processes keep it safe.

badges.meaning: The postmaster accepts the connection and forks a backend for this client.
The backend sends the SQL through parser, rewriter, planner and executor.
The executor reaches table and index pages through access methods and shared buffers.
Every change is written to the WAL log first, which also feeds replicas.
Helpers flush dirty pages (checkpointer) and clean old rows (autovacuum).

title: INSERT then COMMIT
caption: Follow the numbers down: the row is changed in memory, logged, and the WAL is flushed before the client hears committed, while the data file is written later.

badges.meaning: Client sends INSERT to its backend.
Backend parses, plans and runs the query.
Backend adds the row to a page in shared buffers.
Backend logs the change as a WAL record.
Backend flushes WAL to disk, so the commit is durable.
Backend tells the client the commit worked.
Later, a background process writes the changed page to the data file.

title: The data directory layout
caption: Everything the server stores lives under one folder (PGDATA): settings, table files in base/ and global/, and safety records in pg_wal/ and pg_xact/.
